6: [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/go-simpler/sloglint/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/go-simpler/sloglint)
7: 
8: A Go linter that ensures consistent code style when using `log/slog`.
9: 
10: ## 📌 About
11: 
12: The `log/slog` API allows two different types of arguments: key-value pairs and attributes.
13: While people may have different opinions about which one is better, most seem to agree on one thing: it should be consistent.
14: With `sloglint` you can enforce various rules for `log/slog` based on your preferred code style.
15: 
16: ## 🚀 Features
17: 
18: * Enforce not mixing key-value pairs and attributes (default)
19: * Enforce using either key-value pairs only or attributes only (optional)
20: * Enforce not using global loggers (optional)
21: * Enforce using methods that accept a context (optional)
22: * Enforce using static log messages (optional)
23: * Enforce using constants instead of raw keys (optional)
24: * Enforce a single key naming convention (optional)
25: * Enforce not using specific keys (optional)
26: * Enforce putting arguments on separate lines (optional)
27: 
28: ## 📦 Install
29: 
30: `sloglint` is integrated into [`golangci-lint`][1], and this is the recommended way to use it.
31: 
32: To enable the linter, add the following lines to `.golangci.yml`:
33: 
34: ```yaml
35: linters:
36:   enable:
37:     - sloglint
38: ```
39: 
40: Alternatively, you can download a prebuilt binary from the [Releases][2] page to use `sloglint` standalone.
41: 
42: ## 📋 Usage
43: 
44: Run `golangci-lint` with `sloglint` enabled.
45: See the list of [available options][3] to configure the linter.
46: 
47: When using `sloglint` standalone, pass the options as flags of the same name.
48: 
49: ### No mixed arguments
50: 
51: The `no-mixed-args` option causes `sloglint` to report mixing key-values pairs and attributes within a single function call:
52: 
53: ```go
54: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "user_id", 42, slog.String("ip_address", "192.0.2.0")) // sloglint: key-value pairs and attributes should not be mixed
55: ```
56: 
57: It is enabled by default.
58: 
59: ### Key-value pairs only
60: 
61: The `kv-only` option causes `sloglint` to report any use of attributes:
62: 
63: ```go
64: slog.Info("a user has logged in", slog.Int("user_id", 42)) // sloglint: attributes should not be used
65: ```
66: 
67: ### Attributes only
68: 
69: In contrast, the `attr-only` option causes `sloglint` to report any use of key-value pairs:
70: 
71: ```go
72: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "user_id", 42) // sloglint: key-value pairs should not be used
73: ```
74: 
75: ### No global
76: 
77: Some projects prefer to pass loggers as explicit dependencies.
78: The `no-global` option causes `sloglint` to report the use of global loggers.
79: 
80: ```go
81: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "user_id", 42) // sloglint: global logger should not be used
82: ```
83: 
84: Possible values are `all` (report all global loggers) and `default` (report only the default `slog` logger).
85: 
86: ### Context only
87: 
88: Some `slog.Handler` implementations make use of the given `context.Context` (e.g. to access context values).
89: For them to work properly, you need to pass a context to all logger calls.
90: The `context-only` option causes `sloglint` to report the use of methods without a context:
91: 
92: ```go
93: slog.Info("a user has logged in") // sloglint: InfoContext should be used instead
94: ```
95: 
96: Possible values are `all` (report all contextless calls) and `scope` (report only if a context exists in the scope of the outermost function).
97: 
98: ### Static messages
99: 
100: To get the most out of structured logging, you may want to require log messages to be static.
101: The `static-msg` option causes `sloglint` to report non-static messages:
102: 
103: ```go
104: slog.Info(fmt.Sprintf("a user with id %d has logged in", 42)) // sloglint: message should be a string literal or a constant
105: ```
106: 
107: The report can be fixed by moving dynamic values to arguments:
108: 
109: ```go
110: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "user_id", 42)
111: ```
112: 
113: ### No raw keys
114: 
115: To prevent typos, you may want to forbid the use of raw keys altogether.
116: The `no-raw-keys` option causes `sloglint` to report the use of strings as keys
117: (including `slog.Attr` calls, e.g. `slog.Int("user_id", 42)`):
118: 
119: ```go
120: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "user_id", 42) // sloglint: raw keys should not be used
121: ```
122: 
123: This report can be fixed by using either constants...
124: 
125: ```go
126: const UserId = "user_id"
127: 
128: slog.Info("a user has logged in", UserId, 42)
129: ```
130: 
131: ...or custom `slog.Attr` constructors:
132: 
133: ```go
134: func UserId(value int) slog.Attr { return slog.Int("user_id", value) }
135: 
136: slog.Info("a user has logged in", UserId(42))
137: ```
138: 
139: > [!TIP]
140: > Such helpers can be automatically generated for you by the [`sloggen`][4] tool. Give it a try too!
141: 
142: ### Key naming convention
143: 
144: To ensure consistency in logs, you may want to enforce a single key naming convention.
145: The `key-naming-case` option causes `sloglint` to report keys written in a case other than the given one:
146: 
147: ```go
148: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "user-id", 42) // sloglint: keys should be written in snake_case
149: ```
150: 
151: Possible values are `snake`, `kebab`, `camel`, or `pascal`.
152: 
153: ### Forbidden keys
154: 
155: To prevent accidental use of reserved log keys, you may want to forbid specific keys altogether.
156: The `forbidden-keys` option causes `sloglint` to report the use of forbidden keys:
157: 
158: ```go
159: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "reserved", 42) // sloglint: "reserved" key is forbidden and should not be used
160: ```
161: 
162: For example, when using the standard `slog.JSONHandler` and `slog.TextHandler`,
163: you may want to forbid the `time`, `level`, `msg`, and `source` keys, as these are used by the handlers.
164: 
165: ### Arguments on separate lines
166: 
167: To improve code readability, you may want to put arguments on separate lines, especially when using key-value pairs.
168: The `args-on-sep-lines` option causes `sloglint` to report 2+ arguments on the same line:
169: 
170: ```go
171: slog.Info("a user has logged in", "user_id", 42, "ip_address", "192.0.2.0") // sloglint: arguments should be put on separate lines
172: ```
173: 
174: This report can be fixed by reformatting the code:
175: 
176: ```go
177: slog.Info("a user has logged in",
178:     "user_id", 42,
179:     "ip_address", "192.0.2.0",
180: )
181: ```
